claims.text: Controlled annealing or other thermal processing can refine the grain size of a FeNiCrCoCu thin coating.
Reducing the initial grain size of FeNiCrCoCu coatings promotes dynamic amorphization during high-temperature sliding.
Dynamic amorphization during sliding produces an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The ultra-nanocrystalline layer localizes shear at high-angle grain boundaries.
Formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer is associated with low friction and high wear resistance in a CoCrFeMnNi HEA under ultra-high vacuum.
The ultra-nanocrystalline layer confines microscopic deformation in FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Confining deformation in the near-surface layer limits the propagation of plastic damage.
Inverse Hall-Petch behavior and grain-size-dependent shear strength have been observed or modeled in a CoCrFeMnNi HEA.
The proposed FeNiCrCoCu deformation mechanism resembles inverse Hall-Petch behavior in other HEAs.
A grain-refined FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a lower wear rate than the coarse-grained baseline.
A grain-refined FeNiCrCoCu coating will exhibit shallower and more localized microscopic deformation than the coarse-grained baseline.
A grain-refined FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a lower coefficient of friction than the coarse-grained baseline.
The coarse-grained baseline is less capable of forming a protective ultra-nanocrystalline layer during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted behavior is limited to high-temperature sliding in an inert or non-oxidizing environment.
Oxidizing conditions may produce a different wear mechanism because oxidation and mixed metal-oxide films are no longer mitigated.
Cu may modify the dynamic-amorphization response of FeNiCrCoCu relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
